note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Three days of diarrhea (loose, watery stool) with frequent bathroom visits (6–7 times/day).
  - Associated left lower abdominal crampy pain; feeling weak and hot (feverish).
  - Vomiting at the start of symptoms, now resolved.
  - Loss of appetite; able to drink fluids; consuming soups, smoothies, and liquid foods.
  - Possible trigger: Chinese takeaway meal about four days ago.
  - Family exposure: no other family members with the same symptoms.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Symptoms began three days ago; started with vomiting, now primarily diarrhea with cramps and weakness; feverish sensation noted at onset (3–4 days ago); condition affecting daily activities and work.
- ENT symptoms:
  - None (no throat/voice/nasal/ocular symptoms reported; no stridor or dyspnea).
- Past medical history and treatments:
  - Asthma, well-controlled with inhaler.
  - No other chronic illnesses reported.
  - Prior ED visits/hospitalizations not noted.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Current medications: asthma inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); no other medications.
- Social context:
  - Occupation: accountant.
  - Lives with wife and two children.
  - Not stated whether accompanied to visit.

Objective:
- Observable findings:
  - No ENT swelling or observable airway/neck findings described.
  - No vitals recorded.
  - No physical examination findings documented.
- Additional notes:
  - Not recorded if another person was present with the patient during the visit.

Assessment:
- Primary impression: Suspected gastroenteritis (likely viral) presenting with diarrhea, initial vomiting, abdominal cramps (left lower quadrant), feverish sensation, and weakness; recent takeaway food exposure (Chinese restaurant) reported.
- Justification from transcript: onset within ~3 days, loose watery stools, abdominal cramp, feverish feeling, prior vomiting, absence of blood in stool/vomit, recent food exposure, asthma history but currently controlled; no ENT symptoms.

Plan:
- Immediate management:
  - Conservative management with hydration and oral rehydration.
  - Recommend Dioralyte (electrolyte rehydration) to replenish minerals; dose/frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol for fever/weakness: two tablets up to four times daily; route not documented.
  - Advise taking time off work for 2–3 days to rest while infection clears.
  - No antibiotics indicated at this time.
- Follow-up and escalation:
  - If symptoms do not improve, re-evaluate in 3–4 days.
  - Consider stool sample testing if symptoms persist to exclude alternative etiologies.
- Education and instructions:
  - Maintain oral fluids; continue light foods as tolerated.
  - Return sooner if worsening symptoms (inability to keep fluids down, dehydration signs, high fever, blood in stool, persistent vomiting, or new ENT symptoms like throat closing or breathing difficulty).
- Additional notes:
  - No ENT-specific referrals or vaccination discussions indicated.
  - No COVID-19 vaccine considerations documented.
